Consumer Non-Cyclicals: Consumer Non-Cyclicals posted a robust average annual earnings growth of 32.27% over the past year, positioning the sector ninth among fifteen sectors in earnings expansion. Revenue rose at a more modest pace of 9.71% on average, earning a sixth place ranking for revenue growth. Within the group, [#VC2.SI]Olam Group Ltd[\#VC2.SI] delivered the strongest yearly earnings surge, while [#EB5.SI]First Resources Ltd[\#EB5.SI] led the sector in revenue increase. The sector’s performance is bolstered by Singapore’s high per capita consumption of food and personal care products and by the island’s strict food safety regulations that favor established local suppliers. Additionally, limited exposure to cyclical demand fluctuations helps sustain steady sales even when broader consumer sentiment shifts.
Consumer Cyclicals: Despite a modest decline in earnings, the Consumer Cyclicals sector posted an average annual earnings growth of -3.93%, placing it twelfth among fifteen sectors for earnings expansion. In contrast, revenue grew strongly at an average annual rate of 14.9%, earning the sector the second best rank for revenue growth. The sector’s revenue boost is helped by Singapore’s rising household disposable income and the seasonal surge in retail activity around local festivals, which drive higher consumer spending on discretionary goods. Meanwhile, tighter credit conditions and higher input costs have limited profit margins, contributing to the negative earnings trend. Within the sector, [#51O.SI]MSM International Ltd[\#51O.SI] delivered the strongest yearly earnings growth, while [#5OX.SI]Mary Chia Holdings Ltd[\#5OX.SI] achieved the highest revenue growth.
Transportation & Logistics: Transportation & Logistics recorded modest earnings growth of 1.81% and revenue growth of 2.7% over the past year. The sector ranked 11th out of 15 for both earnings and revenue growth, indicating it lagged behind most other sectors. [#FQ7.SI]Salt Investments Ltd[\#FQ7.SI] delivered the strongest earnings expansion within the group, while [#R14.SI]Eneco Energy Ltd[\#R14.SI] posted the highest revenue increase. Growth was shaped by Singapore’s role as a regional transshipment hub, where expanding container volumes at the port and tighter berth allocations pressured margins. At the same time, government incentives for digital freight platforms and stricter emissions standards for trucks added both opportunities and cost pressures. These Singapore-specific dynamics tempered the sector’s overall performance despite the positive top-company results.
Healthcare: Despite a modest revenue increase, the Healthcare sector posted a sharp decline in earnings, with an average annual earnings growth of minus 79.42 percent and an average annual revenue growth of 13.16 percent. This places the sector near the bottom of earnings performance, ranking fourteenth out of fifteen sectors, while its revenue growth ranks fourth among all sectors. The strongest earnings expansion came from [#FHH.SI]FHH[\#FHH.SI], which recorded the highest yearly earnings growth within the sector, and [#8YY.SI]Embracing Future Holdings Ltd[\#8YY.SI] led revenue growth with the biggest yearly increase. Growth in the sector is further shaped by Singapore’s stringent drug approval process and the government’s emphasis on expanding public health infrastructure, which can limit short term profitability but support longer term demand. Consequently, investors see a divergence between revenue expansion driven by rising healthcare utilization and earnings pressure from regulatory and cost factors.
Properties & Real Estate: Properties & Real Estate delivered an average annual earnings growth of 84.11% over the past year, placing the sector third among fifteen sectors for earnings expansion. Revenue grew at an average annual rate of 13.4%, also ranking the sector third for revenue growth. [#5IC.SI][#5IC.SI]SING Holdings Ltd[\#5IC.SI][\#5IC.SI] led the sector with the highest yearly earnings growth and the highest yearly revenue growth. The sector’s performance was shaped by Singapore’s limited land availability, which continues to drive premium pricing for existing assets, and by recent government cooling measures that have tempered new development while encouraging the conversion of older properties. Additionally, tighter financing conditions for developers and a modest influx of foreign buyers have uniquely influenced growth dynamics in the local market.
Energy: The Energy sector posted a contraction in earnings, with an average annual decline of 8.4%, while revenue grew modestly by 0.5% over the same period. This performance places the sector 13th out of 15 for earnings growth and 14th out of 15 for revenue growth, indicating weaker momentum compared with most other sectors. Within the sector, [#JFQ.SI]JFQ[\#JFQ.SI] recorded the highest yearly earnings growth, and [#TPED.SI]PTT Exploration Production PCL DRC[\#TPED.SI] delivered the strongest yearly revenue growth. Growth in Singapore's Energy segment is uniquely constrained by the country's reliance on imported crude, strict carbon‑pricing regulations, and limited domestic hydrocarbon reserves, which together temper both profitability and top‑line expansion. The combination of these market‑specific factors and the sector’s low rankings underscores the challenges facing energy companies operating in Singapore.
Utilities: The Utilities sector posted a striking earnings surge, with an average annual earnings growth of about 49.96%, placing it fourth among fifteen sectors for earnings expansion. Despite this strong profit momentum, average annual revenue fell by roughly 5.5%, the lowest revenue growth ranking at fifteenth out of the same fifteen sectors. [#5GD.SI]Sunpower Group Ltd[\#5GD.SI] delivered the highest earnings growth within the sector, while [#BEH.SI]China International Holdings Ltd[\#BEH.SI] recorded the strongest revenue increase. Growth dynamics are shaped by Singapore’s regulated tariff framework, which can boost profitability when rates are adjusted but also constrain top‑line expansion, and by the nation’s aggressive renewable‑energy targets that require significant capital investment in grid upgrades and new generation assets.
Consumer Defensive: The Consumer Defensive sector posted an impressive average annual earnings growth of 46.8% over the past year, placing it fifth among fifteen sectors for earnings expansion. Its average annual revenue grew by 10.86%, also ranking fifth for revenue growth across the peer group. Within the sector, [#CNE.SI]MindChamps PreSchool Ltd[\#CNE.SI] delivered the strongest earnings acceleration, while [#5EG.SI]Zhongxin Fruit and Juice Ltd[\#5EG.SI] led the revenue surge. Growth has been bolstered by Singapore’s strong demand for essential household products and the continued emphasis on early childhood education, which drives spending on services that are less sensitive to economic cycles. Additionally, the sector benefits from a stable supply chain for locally sourced food and beverage items, supporting revenue gains despite broader market fluctuations.
Financial Services: Over the past year the Financial Services sector posted an average earnings growth of 8.96% and an average revenue growth of 8.69%. This placed the sector tenth in earnings growth and eighth in revenue growth among the fifteen SGX sectors. [#I49.SI]IFS Capital Ltd[\#I49.SI] delivered the strongest earnings expansion, while [#K6S.SI]Prudential PLC[\#K6S.SI] led the sector in revenue growth. Growth was further supported by Singapore’s progressive regulatory framework that encourages fintech innovation and by the continued inflow of regional wealth seeking local wealth‑management services. At the same time, the Monetary Authority of Singapore’s prudential guidelines on capital adequacy have prompted banks to optimise balance sheets, adding to the sector’s overall performance.
Communication Services: The Communication Services sector posted a sharp contraction in earnings, with an average annual earnings decline of 116.57%. This placed the sector at the bottom of the fifteen‑sector ranking for earnings growth. Conversely, revenue grew modestly by 2.9% on average, earning the sector the tenth spot out of fifteen for revenue growth. [#9VW.SI][#9VW.SI]Spackman Entertainment Group Ltd[\#9VW.SI][\#9VW.SI] led the sector, delivering the highest yearly earnings growth as well as the strongest revenue expansion among its peers. In Singapore, the sector’s performance is shaped by the recent tightening of broadcast licensing rules and the rollout of 5G spectrum, which have increased capital spending for telecom operators while limiting new entrants, thereby suppressing earnings but supporting modest top‑line growth. Overall, the sector’s earnings outlook remains pressured despite incremental revenue gains.
Basic Materials: The Basic Materials sector posted an extraordinary earnings growth of about 1197.7% over the past year, the highest among the fifteen SGX sectors. Its average annual revenue rose 9.17%, placing the sector seventh in revenue growth rankings. [#KUO.SI]International Cement Group Ltd[\#KUO.SI] drove the earnings surge, recording the strongest yearly increase within the sector, while [#C8R.SI]Jiutian Chemical Group Ltd[\#C8R.SI] led revenue expansion with the top yearly gain. Growth has been further supported by Singapore’s ongoing infrastructure upgrades, which boost demand for cement and construction aggregates, and by the country’s strategic port facilities that streamline the import of raw minerals essential for chemical production. These Singapore‑specific dynamics have helped amplify the sector’s performance beyond broader market trends.
Infrastructures: Over the past year the Infrastructures sector posted an extraordinary average annual earnings growth of about 341.48%, placing it second among the fifteen SGX sectors for earnings expansion. By contrast, its average annual revenue grew modestly by roughly 1.75%, which ranks the sector thirteenth for revenue growth. [#Z74.SI]Singapore Telecommunications Ltd[\#Z74.SI] delivered the strongest earnings surge within the sector, while [#S59.SI]SIA Engineering Co Ltd[\#S59.SI] recorded the highest revenue increase. Growth in the sector is further driven by Singapore’s ongoing large‑scale public‑infrastructure programmes, such as new transport links and digital backbone upgrades, which create demand for telecom and engineering services. At the same time, the sector faces tight land availability and stringent environmental regulations that shape investment decisions uniquely for infrastructure projects in the city‑state.
REIT: Over the past year the REIT sector posted an average earnings growth of 37.47%, placing it eighth among fifteen sectors for earnings expansion. Revenue grew at a more modest 4.12% on average, which ranked the sector ninth for revenue growth. [#M1GU.SI]Alpha Integrated REIT[\#M1GU.SI] delivered the strongest earnings acceleration within the group, while [#DCRU.SI]Digital Core REIT[\#DCRU.SI] led the sector in revenue growth. The sector’s performance is shaped by Singapore’s limited land supply and the government’s cautious approach to REIT leverage, which together influence acquisition opportunities and financing costs. Additionally, strong demand for logistics and data-centre space has supported rental income, while the local interest-rate environment has a direct impact on distribution yields. These market-specific dynamics help explain the divergence between robust earnings growth and slower revenue expansion.
Industrials: Over the past year the Industrials sector posted an average earnings growth of 43.5%, placing it sixth among the fifteen SGX sectors for earnings expansion. Revenue in the same period rose by 2.34% on average, which ranks the sector twelfth for revenue growth. The strong earnings surge is driven in part by [#5OC.SI]Koyo International Ltd[\#5OC.SI], which recorded the highest yearly earnings growth within the sector, while [#Y06.SI]Green Build Technology Ltd[\#Y06.SI] led the sector in revenue growth. In Singapore, the sector benefits from continued government investment in port infrastructure and the expansion of industrial estates that support logistics and manufacturing activities. These sector-specific developments help sustain the earnings momentum even as revenue growth remains modest.
Technology: Singapore’s Technology sector posted an average annual earnings growth of 42.37% over the past year, positioning it seventh among fifteen sectors for earnings expansion. Revenue in the sector grew by 16.97% on average, which is the strongest rate, earning the top rank for revenue growth. The sector’s performance is bolstered by Singapore’s aggressive push for a nationwide 5G rollout and incentives for data center investments, which uniquely benefit technology firms.
